receipt.public_excerpt: performance of LLMs deteriorating as question complexity increases.

evidence_items.explanation: The study evaluated 25 models using repeated template-generated questions and controlled changes. It reports recurring sensitivity to complexity and irrelevant clauses, supporting a systematic mathematical-robustness problem across tested models.

evidence_items.publisher: arXiv; Karthik Valmeekam, Kaya Stechly and Subbarao Kambhampati
evidence_items.locator: Accuracy with Increased Problem Size; preceding planning results and Table 2
evidence_items.explanation: The study reports 97.8% accuracy for o1-preview on 600 simpler Blocksworld instances, but 23.63% on 110 larger instances, alongside degradation under obfuscation. This supports recurring planning weaknesses while also documenting substantial improvement and strong performance in an easier setting.

evidence_items.locator: Section 1, Introduction, summary of evaluation findings
evidence_items.explanation: This independent study evaluated 25 models and four prompting techniques using 10,552 question variations. Its recurring failures under mathematical perturbations provide corroboration beyond Apple's study.

receipt.public_excerpt: nearly always proposed a legal move.

evidence_items.explanation: Specialized fine-tuning produced strong move-legality performance, qualifying any general inference from chess anecdotes. These small, task-specialized models and single-move tests do not directly refute recurring failures in the general-purpose models discussed by Marcus.

evidence_items.locator: TL;DR; methodology and discussion provide qualifications
evidence_items.explanation: A later experiment, including a 2024 GPT-4o snapshot, reports that auditing ambiguous distractors substantially reduces performance drops. It used newly generated distractors rather than Apple's original NoOp set and occurred outside the target period, so it qualifies the interpretation without directly overturning the historical findings.
